intentions.title: Deliver one control plane for 'one login, one dashboard, for all your Barkparks' — identity, provisioning, and billing unified across a fleet of independently-hosted instances
intentions.evidence: accounts.ex: single User + Team membership fans identity out across every registered instance; registry.ex: Barkpark/Provider/AgentEvent/AgentToken all Team-scoped so one team never sees another's instances; router.ex moduledoc frames this as the JSON API the dashboard SPA, Go CLI, and on-box agents all share.

intentions.title: Run the control plane as a minimal Plug.Router JSON API — never Phoenix/LiveView — deliberately decoupled from the OSS Barkpark Studio stack
intentions.evidence: web/router.ex moduledoc: 'Deliberately NOT Phoenix/LiveView'; application.ex boots Bandit directly with BarkparkCloud.Web.Router as the plug, gated by config `server:` for test isolation via Plug.Test.

intentions.title: Gate managed infrastructure strictly behind entitlement — pay-once go-live, dunning grace, and suspend/resume tied to real Stripe subscription state, built and testable at €0 spend
intentions.evidence: billing.ex: gateway() indirection (StubGateway vs real Stripe), entitled?/1 checks active OR past_due-within-grace, @grace_days 3-day dunning window, cancel_subscription/1 SUSPENDS managed instances while recover_subscription/1 RESUMES them; router.ex POST /v1/go-live 'gate on active subscription'.

intentions.title: Make every usage/health meter on the dashboard honest — a meter with no real ceiling never draws a quota bar, and the full meter vocabulary is always present even when inputs fail
intentions.evidence: usage.ex moduledoc: 'meters without truth are lies' (epic charter D48); compose/1 documented PURE and TOTAL (never touches network/DB, never raises, always emits fixed vocabulary); three explicit quota/threshold families (billing quota vs physical percent vs rate-with-no-quota).

intentions.title: Provision and operate a fleet of Barkpark instances (and their Sites/Deployments) through an off-box worker/agent/builder protocol with atomic claim, lease expiry, and stale-job reaping — no job silently stuck or double-run
intentions.evidence: registry.ex: claim_next_job/1 with @default_stale_after_seconds (12min, sized above the Go worker's 8min timeout), @default_max_provision_attempts cap, reap_stale_deployments; router.ex /v1/internal/provision-jobs/* and /v1/builder/* and /v1/agent/* claim/transition/console/detail endpoints; failure_copy.ex humanizes the resulting raw failure jargon for every read surface.

intentions.title: Fold three disjoint bearer-token principals (user session, on-box agent, shared worker secret) into one Authorization header contract, each with its own store and fail-closed default
intentions.evidence: web/auth.ex moduledoc: require_user / require_agent / require_worker pipelines against separate stores; require_worker 'fails CLOSED' when no WORKER_TOKEN is configured rather than opening internal endpoints to all.

intentions.title: Let a team stand up managed sites via a real GitHub connection (App install, repo picker, push-triggered deploys) while the app remains fully bootable with GitHub entirely unconfigured
intentions.evidence: github.ex moduledoc: 'HUMAN-LAST / fail-closed' — configured?/0 gates a 503 feature_not_configured, GitHub.Fake client used in dev/test, app 'BOOTS regardless (plugins-off philosophy)'; router.ex /v1/github/* + /v1/sites/:id/github/connect + /v1/webhooks/github/:site_id (HMAC-verified push → Deployment).

intentions.title: Reach every team member over email without ever leaking data cross-team or requiring SMTP setup before onboarding — settings-encrypted-at-rest, alert dispatch always team-scoped, transactional mail always on the platform mailer
intentions.evidence: notifications.ex moduledoc: recipients 'ALWAYS team members' (mirrors Coolify's EmailChannel data-exfiltration guard), SMTP secrets run through Registry.Vault.encrypt/1 before the changeset, settings_view/1 masks ciphertext, transactional mail 'ALWAYS ride the platform BarkparkCloud.Mailer'.
